texts.preamble: Deepanshu vs Sri Om on 9 September, 2025 In The Court Of Sh. Sachin Gupta, Presiding Officer:Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-02, West, Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi Mact Case No. 943/2018 Dlwt010113382018 Sh. Deepanshu S/o Sh. Jitender R/o H. No. 279, Panna Barsan, Village & Post Office, Tikri Kalan, Delhi-110041 .....Petitioner Versus 1. Sri Om S/o Sh. Kishan Chand R/o 158, Mandir Wali Gali, Baba Haridass Nagar Colony, Tikri Border, Delhi-110041 2. The New India Assurance Company Limited Office at: 902, Hemkunt House-6, Rajendra Place, Delhi-110008 ..... Respondents Date of Institution : 15.12.2018 Date of reserving order/judgment : 02.09.2025 Date of pronouncement : 09.09.2025 Awar D 1.
texts.facts: As per the facts mentioned in the claim petition as well as documents annexed therewith, on 27.03.2018 at about 5:30 PM to 6 PM, while the petitioner was going on his Scooty TVS Jupiter bearing registration no. DL8SBM7585, from Tikri Kalan towards Bahadurgarh City and when he reached near Metro Pillar No. 799, opposite Metro Depot, Rohtak Deepanshu vs Sri Om on 9 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48801627/ 1 Road, Tehsil Bahadurgarh, District Jhajjar, Haryana, suddenly, a Tractor bearing registration no. HR-13H-4273 (hereinafter referred to as 'offending vehicle'), which was being driven by respondent no. 1 in wrong side and in rash and negligent manner and at high speed, hit against the scooty of the petitioner from front side and due to forceful impact of hitting, the petitioner fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries and fracture on many parts of his whole body and his scooty was also badly damaged. It is further stated that respondent no. 1 ran away from the spot and petitioner was taken to Civil Hospital, Bahadurgarh, wherein he received first aid and thereafter, admitted in the Sri Balaji Action Medical Institute, Paschim Vihar, New Delhi, wherein he was medically examined vide MLR no. 7423 and he remained hospitalized from 27.03.2018 to 09.04.2018. It is further stated that a FIR no. 183/2018 PS City Bahadurgarh, District Jhajjar, Haryana, U/s 279/337/338 IPC was also got registered regarding this accident. 2. As per the claim petition, the respondent no. 1 is the driver-cum-owner of the offending vehicle, which was insured with respondent no. 2 i.e. The New India Assurance Company Digitally signed by SACHIN SACHIN GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2025.09.09 16:39:57 +0530 MACT No. 943/2018 Date of Award: 09.09.2025 Limited. 3. In its written statement filed on behalf of respondent no. 1, it is stated inter alia that no alleged accident took place with the vehicle of the answering respondent; that the respondent has not caused the alleged accident; that the alleged accident took place due to sole negligence of the petitioner while driving his vehicle i.e. Scooty no. DL8SBM7585, who drove the same in negligent manner, high speed without observing traffic rules; that the petition is bad for misjoinder and non joinder of necessary parties i.e. owner and insurance company of the scooty; that answering respondent is not responsible or liable for the alleged accident and vehicle in question was fully insured with the respondent no.2 vide policy valid with effect from 23.09.2017 to 22.09.2018 and the petitioner was not having driving license at the time of alleged accident. 4. In its written statement filed on behalf of the respondent no.2/insurance company, it is stated inter alia that the petitioner himself was negligent in causing the accident; that there is a delay of 10 days in lodging the FIR, which has not been explained; that accident was caused by head on collision between alleged offending vehicle and scooty of the petitioner, therefore, injured himself was negligent in causing the accident; that injured was not having driving license; that on the date of accident i.e. 27.03.2018, the vehicle bearing registration no. HR 13H4273 was insured in the name of Sri Om with the answering respondent, however, the liability of the answering respondent, if any, is subject to terms, conditions, limitation and exceptions contained there in and M.V. Act 1988 and Rules framed thereunder and the owner / insured must prove that vehicle in SACHIN GUPTA GUPTA 2025.09.09 16:40:04 +0530 MACT No. 943/2018 Date of Award: 09.09.2025 question had valid RC, Fitness Certificate and Permit for the area where the alleged accident took place. 5. From the pleadings of the parties, following issues were framed by the Ld. Predecessor of this Tribunal on 12.04.2019:- Deepanshu vs Sri Om on 9 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48801627/ 2 OPP 3. Relief. 6. In order to prove his case, petitioner examined four witnesses. PW-1 is petitioner himself who tendered his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.PW1/A; PW2 is Dr. Swati Phuljhele Aalok, Associate Professor, Dr. Rajender Prasad Centre for Ophthalmic Sciences, AIIMS, Ansari Nagar, New Delhi; PW3 is Dr. Naresh Chandra, Specialist and HOD (Ortho) Guru Gobind Singh Government Hospital, Delhi and PW4 is Dr. Prithvi B, Senior Resident, AIIMS, Delhi. The onus to prove this issue was placed on the petitioner. Petitioner/PW-1 tendered his affidavit in evidence Ex.PW1/A and relied upon the documents i.e. (i) Copy of his Aadhar Card Ex.PW1/1 Deepanshu vs Sri Om on 9 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48801627/ 3 (OSR); (ii) Certified copy of challan Ex.PW1/2 and (iii) Original medical record / bills Ex.PW1/3 (Colly). 11. In his cross-examination done by the Ld. counsel for the respondent no.2, PW-1 admitted that at the time of accident, he was driving the scooty. He stated that he was having driving SACHIN GUPTA GUPTA 2025.09.09 16:40:23 +0530 MACT No. 943/2018 Date of Award: 09.09.2025 license, the copy of the same is Ex.PW1/R2. He admitted that DL was issued on 16.08.2018. He further stated that earlier he was issued learning license and subsequent to his learning license, permanent DL was issued, copy of his learning license was marked as Mark Z. He further stated that while he was driving the scooty at the time of accident, he was alone. He admitted that it was a head-on collision. He denied to the suggestion that he was without helmet at the time of accident or that the accident in question took place due to his negligence or that offending vehicle was not at fault or that the offending vehicle was not negligent or that he was driving the scooty without DL. In his cross examination done by the Ld. Counsel for the respondent no.1, he denied to the suggestion that the accident took place due to his negligence as he fell of his own or that no other vehicle was involved in the accident or that he was driving his scooty rashly due to which he could not see the stone on his way and fell down or that he was deposing falsely. 12. PW-1 / petitioner has deposed in lines with the claim petition and has well explained the mode and manner of the accident. From the careful perusal of the testimony of the injured / PW-1 including his cross examination, there is nothing material has been elicited to disbelieve the version of accident as given by PW-1. Rather evidence of PW-1 remained consistent on the aspect of accident, having been caused by rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1 (driver of offending vehicle). He has categorically deposed that the offending vehicle alongwith safety tank being driven by respondent no. 1 in wrong side and in very rash and negligent manner and at high speed, hit against his scooty and due to the forceful impact of the hitting, he Digitally signed by SACHIN SACHIN GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2025.09.09 16:40:31 +0530 MACT No. 943/2018 Date of Award: 09.09.2025 fell down on the road and received grievous injuries. It is evident from the testimony of PW-1 that respondents could not impeach his testimony through litmus test of cross-examination. In the light of the aforementioned judgments, the compensation to which the petitioner is entitled shall be as under:- Medical Expenses: 26. PW-1 i.e. the injured has inter alia deposed in his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.PW1/A that he spent Rs.7,97,506/- on his medical treatment, medicines, hospital expenses, doctor fees, medical tests etc. He has filed on record his original medical bills, which are Ex.PW1/3 (Colly). In his cross examination done by the Ld. Counsel for the respondent no.2, he admitted that he was covered under Park Mediclaim policy and he received Rs.1,50,000/- from the said policy. Thus, a sum of Rs. 24,89,962/- (rounded off) is awarded in favour of petitioner under this head. Special Diet, Conveyance Charges & Attendant Charges: 37. Petitioner (PW1) in his evidence by way of affidavit deposed that he had spent Rs.1,00,000/- on his conveyance, ambulance, special diet and attendant etc so far. In his cross examination done by the Ld. Counsel for the respondent no.2/insurance company, he denied to the suggestion that he had Digitally signed by SACHIN SACHIN GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2025.09.09 16:42:41 +0530 MACT No. 943/2018 Date of Award: 09.09.2025 not incurred any amount on his attendant charges, diet, conveyance or that for this reason only, he had not filed any document in respect of the same. "It is difficult to measure the pain and suffering in terms of money which is suffered by a victim on account of serious injuries caused to him in a motor vehicle accident. Since the compensation is required to be paid for pain and suffering an attempt must be made to award compensation which may have some objective relation with the pain and suffering underwent by the victim. For this purpose, the Claims Tribunal and the Courts normally consider the nature of injury; the part of the body where the injuries were sustained, surgeries, if any, underwent by the victim, confinement in the hospital and the duration of treatment". 39. Petitioner/Injured has deposed that he suffered great pain, mental tension and agony due to this accident. It is evident that petitioner had sustained multiple injuries including permanent disability to the extent of 24% in relation to his left upper and lower limb and permanent visual disability of 40% under category III a, (Low Vision). Ocular testimony is duly corroborated by the medical record as well as disability certificate Ex.PW3/A and Ex.PW4/1 respectively. Thus, he would have undergone great physical sufferings and mental shock on account of the accident in question. Keeping in view the medical treatment record of petitioner available on record, I hereby award a sum of Rs.1,50,000/- towards pain and sufferings to the petitioner. Compensation towards loss of amenities of life 40. As already mentioned above, petitioner had suffered grievous injuries due to the accident in question. He has also sustained permanent disability of 24% in relation to his left upper and lower limb and permanent visual disability of 40% under category IIIa, (Low Vision), which is duly SACHIN Digitally signed by SACHIN GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2025.09.09 16:42:59 +0530 MACT No. 943/2018 Date of Award: 09.09.2025 established from the disability certificates (Ex. PW3/A and Ex.PW4/1). Thus, he would not be able to enjoy general amenities of life after the accident in question, during rest of his life. In view of the nature of injuries including permanent disability suffered by him and his continued treatment, I award a notional sum of Rs.1,50,000/- towards loss of amenities of life to the petitioner. 42. Thus, the compensation awarded to the petitioner is summarized as under:- S Heads of Compensation Amount No. 1.
texts.arguments: Counsel for respondents have argued that the injured was not having any driving license at the time of accident and accident was caused due to his own negligence. Per contra, Ld. Counsel for the petitioner has argued that petitioner was having a learning license at the time of the accident and offending vehicle, which was driven by the respondent no. 1 in wrong side of the road and in rash and negligent manner, hit against the scooty of the petitioner and caused the accident and no negligence can be imputed on the part of the petitioner. Deepanshu vs Sri Om on 9 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48801627/ 4 14. Petitioner has filed copy of his learning license Mark Z, which was valid on the date of accident. However, the mere fact that petitioner was not having a valid driving licence at the time of accident, ipso-facto is not sufficient to hold that accident had either taken place due to the negligence or contributory negligence of petitioner. The petitioner has categorically deposed that accident was caused by the offending vehicle, which was being driven by the respondent no. 1 in the wrong side and in a very rash and negligent manner and in high Digitally signed by SACHIN SACHIN GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2025.09.09 16:40:47 +0530 MACT No. 943/2018 Date of Award: 09.09.2025 speed. It was not even disputed by the respondents that the offending vehicle was not being driven on the wrong side of the road. The fact that offending vehicle was driven on the wrong side of the road is further corroborated from the site plan of the place of accident, which is part of Ex.PW1/2. 17. In the case titled 'Ashok Kumar & Anr. Vs. Karan Bhatia, MAC APP. 271/2018 decided on 26.11.2024" , it has been held by the Hon'ble High Court as under:- "12. Shri Mehtab Singh, the eye witness, may have failed to support the case of the prosecution and turned hostile during the trial, but that does not take away the Deepanshu vs Sri Om on 9 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48801627/ 5 factum of accident and demise of Smt.Surjit Kaur. The investigations were duly carried out which revealed not only the involvement of the vehicle, but also that it was the offending vehicle which was being driven in a rash and negligent manner which resulted in the accident. The manner of accident is also evident from the Site Plan prepared during the criminal investigations. 13. In the case of National Insurance Co.,vs Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it has been held that filing of Chargesheet is sufficient proof of the negligence and involvement of the Offending Vehicle. Similar observations have been made in the case of United India Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Deepak Goel and Ors., 2014 (2) TAC 846 Del, that if the claimant was able to prove the criminal case on record pertaining to involvement of the offending vehicle, whereby the criminal records showing SACHIN GUPTA GUPTA 2025.09.09 16:41:02 +0530 MACT No. 943/2018 Date of Award: 09.09.2025 completion of investigation by the police and filing of Chargesheet under Sections 279/304-A IPC against the driver have been proved, then the documents mentioned above are sufficient to establish the fact that the driver was negligent in causing the accident. Where FIR is lodged, Chargesheet is filed, especially in a case where driver after causing the accident had fled away from the spot, then the documents mentioned above are sufficient to establish the fact that the driver of the offending vehicle was negligent in causing the accident particularly when there was no defence available from his side before the learned Tribunal. 14. Similar observations have been made in the cases of Jamanti Devi and Ors. v. Maheshwar Rai, MAC Appeal no. 831/2015 decided on 19.11.2022. 15. The Apex Court has opined in the judgment of Mangla Ram Vs. The Oriental Insurance Company Ltd, AIR 2018 SC 1900 that the key-point of negligence of the driver as set up by the Claimants, is required to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and not by the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt. Thus, filing of Chargesheet against the driver of the offending vehicle prima facie, points towards the complicity in driving the vehicle negligently and rashly. The subsequent acquittal of the accused may of no effect on the assessment of the liability required in motor vehicle accident cases." A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v. Willoughby (1970) Ac 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid). The scope of compensation in injury cases has been considered by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Mr. R.D. Hattangadi v. M/s Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd., 1995 AIR 755. The relevant extract is as under: "Broadly speaking while fixing an amount of compensation payable to a victim of an accident, the damages have to be assessed separately as pecuniary damages and special damages. Pecuniary damages are those which the victim has actually incurred and which is capable of being calculated in terms of money-, whereas non-pecuniary damages are those which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations. 24. Further, in Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & another (2011) 1 SCC 343, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India laid down general principles for computation of compensation in injury cases. The provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. 35. Further, law is well settled that there should be no departure from the multiplier method in injury cases also [refer: Sandeep Khanuja vs. Atul Dande & Anr., (2017) 3 SCC 351]. As such multiplier to be applied in the present case would be 18 as applicable to age group between 15-20 years, as per settled principle laid down in case of Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009) 6 SCC Deepanshu vs Sri Om on 9 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48801627/ 12 121. Moreover, the law has been well settled by the decisions of Supreme Court in the cases of Sandeep Khanuja (supra) and Erudhaya Priya vs. State Express Transport Corporation Ltd., 2020 SCC OnLine SC 601, that while applying the multiplier method, future prospects on advancement in life and career are also to be taken into consideration. Thus, considering the petitioner being 18 years 4 months of age at the time of accident, an addition of income to the extent of 40% towards future prospects has to be counted. Ld. Counsel for insurance company has sought to avoid liability of the insurance company on the ground that at the time of accident, petitioner was not having permanent valid driving license and also on the ground that only the Tractor was insured and Safety tank which was attached with the tractor at the time of accident was not insured with the respondent no. 2 / Insurance Company and therefore, respondent no. 2/insurance company has no liability to indemnify respondent no. 1 or to pay any amount of compensation to the petitioner. 45. Ld. Counsel for petitioner repelled the aforesaid contention on the ground that neither there was any negligence on the part of injured nor any cogent evidence has been led by insurance company in this regard. He further argued that the accident had occurred due to sole negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle i.e. Tractor bearing registration no. HR13H4273. 46. The petitioner has categorically deposed that accident was caused by the offending vehicle, which was being driven by the respondent no. 1 in the SACHIN GUPTA by SACHIN GUPTA Date: 2025.09.09 16:43:15 +0530 MACT No. 943/2018 Date of Award: 09.09.2025 wrong side and in a very rash and negligent manner and in high speed. While saying so, I am also fortified by the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case titled as "Sudhir Kumar Rana Vs. Surinder Singh & Ors.", IV (2008) ACC 770 (SC). In the case titled "Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Limited Vs. Honnamma and Ors., 2025 SCC Online SC 1027", it is held by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India as under:- "10. The legislation i.e., the MV Act, being beneficial and welfare-oriented in nature [Ningamma v United India Insurance Co. Ltd., (2009) 13 SCC 710; K Ramya v National Insurance Co. Ltd., 2022 SCC OnLine SC 1338, and; Shivaleela v Divisional Manager, United India Insurance Co. Ltd., 2025 SCC OnLine SC 563] and ultimately the root cause of the accident being the tractor, which was insured, this crucial fact cannot be lost sight of. Moreover, this Court is duty-bound to be mindful of the ground realities of our nation and cannot let practicality be overshadowed by technicality." In view of the aforesaid Judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case titled "Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Limited Vs. Honnamma and Ors., 2025 SCC Online SC 1027", the safety tank/tanker was not required to be separately registered with the insurance company, to make the insurance company liable for the payment of compensation. Further, respondent no. 2 / Insurance company Deepanshu vs Sri Om on 9 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48801627/ 17 has also failed to establish on record that offending vehicle was being used for any commercial purpose at the time of accident in question.
